docs.description: Proof of concept session guide — Sonos zone picker, iHeart search/browse/playback, favorites. Pre-session checklist, Flask routes, SwiftUI screens, iHeart and Sonos API notes.
Full product context — architecture, stack, features, brand, design principles, marketing positioning, and decision log. Source of truth for all sessions.
Complete feature reference across 10 product areas. Every feature in user-action language with configurable items, status, priority, and audio quality context.
Feature-by-feature comparison vs Roon with Sorriva positioning response. 11 Sorriva advantages, 2 honest gaps, 7 parity features.
Lossless vs hi-res explained. Streaming service quality table. Sorriva delivery path matrix by protocol and hardware.
Cross-product session conventions — start checklist, iteration workflow, session close, zip spec, manifest schemas, rollback, Hub workflow.

Complete Sonos UPnP/SOAP API reference. Discovery, topology, transport, volume, EQ, zone grouping, station playback. Includes S2 firmware quirks (x-rincon: single colon, IdleState behavior, Arc Ultra extended EQ). Validated against live hardware July 2026.

Undocumented iHeart API endpoints. Station info, stream URLs, logo URLs, now-playing limitations. Includes Sonos playback integration (hls-radio:// prefix, DIDL-Lite metadata). Reverse-engineered July 2026.

How Sorriva streams local FLAC to Sonos via iPad HTTP proxy. Research, ruled-out approaches, chosen architecture, Core Transfer flow, quality preservation, what was built (NWListener, 1MB chunks, UNAS Pro findings), known issues. v2.0 updated 2026-07-15.

Markdown version of the local playback architecture doc. Drop into a Claude session as a document upload for efficient reading. Same content as the HTML version — includes all UNAS Pro discoveries, 1MB chunk solution, known short-snippet issue, and next steps.
Highest-authority engineering instruction set for Sorriva. Product principles, architectural invariants, scope controls, operating rules, and definition of done. Governs all AI agent behavior.

Target module boundaries, system shape, persistence model, concurrency model, and correctness changes required. AppEnvironment, PlaybackStore, EndpointDriver, LibraryRepository, SourceResolver, and MusicDomain specifications.
15 work packages in dependency order from correctness baseline through UI redesign. Each package lists affected files, implementation tasks, and acceptance criteria.

12 accepted ADRs covering platform ownership, standalone operation, canonical identity, PlaybackStore authority, endpoint drivers, Keychain, and composition root. Approved implementation patterns A–H. Prohibited patterns list.

Current product state, confirmed defects S-001 through S-006, architecture implementation status table, milestone execution order A–F, and deferred backlog. Updated at session close after each completed work package.

PassioneUI and SorrivaMusicUI module definitions, token contract, design language with approved color palette and typography, component catalog, navigation framework, screen contract, and AI implementation rules.

Complete context transfer for continuing scanner/artwork/NAS reliability work. Full reasoning trail for fScannerIdentityIntegrity, bArtworkSelectionNotBestWins, and the NWError 12 connection-leak investigation (Stage 1 done, Stage 2 not started). Written for a fresh Claude session with zero prior context.

Full chronology of the zone station-name staleness saga and the confirmed architectural root cause: action functions (transfer/group/station-play) mutate raw zone state instead of authoritatively declaring what's playing to the store. Includes what was tried and rejected, so it isn't re-attempted. Design not yet finalized — discuss with Tom before implementing.

Honest, tiered audit of what's actually verified vs merely marked done ahead of the 7-day reliability gate. Surfaces bMissingTracksInAlbum and bScannerTestSeam as previously-unconnected High-priority gaps found via a full roadmap pass. Recommends next diagnostic steps before trusting the gate clock.
